text:
Martin Pospisil is the Flames' resident irritant, and this season he's adding enough hockey to the irritation to matter. After playing only 22 games last season, he has three goals and seven points in 18, five of those points in his last ten, at about 14 minutes a night. Markerzone's headlines from the Seattle game tell you the rest of his job description: he stirred it up again, and Brandon Montour made him pay.

His own finishing is right on his chances, so the points look honest. The line hasn't been as good as the scoring suggests, with Calgary taking 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, though teammates have shot a little cold around him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in a small 2025-26 sample, with the context that he plays with weak teammates against strong opponents. The Calgary Herald's Steinberg column credited Craig Conroy's patience with Pospisil and Adam Klapka. That patience is starting to look right. He needs to keep the chances against down to stay in the lineup when everyone's healthy.
